sourceTitle: UberBond Outbound Genome: Evidence-First Research for Quality-Preserving Industrial Cold Outreach
objective: Build an evidence-first decision system for quality-preserving industrial outbound. 100000/day is a capacity horizon, never a quota.

confidenceLegend.M: useful observational/practitioner evidence with material confounding

strongestFindings.claim: 100k/day should be a capacity ceiling, never a quota; utilization contracts when qualified inventory, legal eligibility, sender health or recipient tolerance contracts.
Optimize qualified positive reply through qualified meeting, opportunity and cleared revenue rather than send count, opens or raw replies.
Gong reported 28M+ cold emails with top 10% performers booking 8.1x as many meetings and receiving 4.2x as many replies as average performers.
At or below 100 words and roughly 3-4 sentences is a strong first-touch prior.
Gong 85M+ displayed reply bins of approximately 2.3% under 50 words, 2.6% at 51-100, 2.0% at 101-150 and 1.6% at 151-200; association is not causation.
Product/pitch language was associated with materially lower replies; buyer language, priorities and relevant proof are stronger priors.
Gong 85M+ reported relative reply associations around +28% make-an-offer, +7% ask-interest, -29% ask-prospect-to-articulate-problem and -44% direct-meeting-ask.
Personalization is multidimensional and differs by seniority across individual, company, activity and industry context.
Company-level context appears relatively more useful for senior buyers while individual/workflow context appears relatively stronger lower in the hierarchy.
Activity/intent is a strong predictive targeting signal but warmth confounds the copy effect of mentioning it.
C-suite requires a distinct policy; Gong 2026 reported executives 30.2% less likely to reply than non-executives and favored concise priority-level evidence-backed messages.
Very short subjects are a strong prior, but tactics that increase opens can reduce downstream reply quality.
30MPC contributes a testable mechanism: strongest plausible trigger linked to problem, minimal credible mechanism and low-friction CTA.
Josh Braun low-friction CTA doctrine agrees directionally with offer/interest-first evidence.
Follow-up matters; Gong/30MPC reported roughly 70% of replies after the first touch and a 6-7 email region before sharp diminishing returns.
No well-supported universal cadence exists; adaptive behavior-triggered sequencing should be tested.
Multichannel deserves testing, not blind adoption; public causal controls are limited.
Channel interactions can reverse local metrics; voicemail may hurt later call connect while helping later email reply in one large observational study.
Segment-specific models are mandatory because large benchmark results vary by department, seniority and industry.
Lavender finance slice reported about 3.2% overall reply versus 5.7% among vendor-defined 90+ scoring emails; useful but commercially conflicted and non-causal.
At Gmail bulk scale, authentication, DNS/PTR, TLS, DMARC alignment and applicable one-click unsubscribe are governance constraints.
Google recommends user-reported spam below 0.1% and avoiding 0.3% or higher; Yahoo also publishes a 0.3% bulk complaint threshold.
There is no global B2B-cold-email-is-legal rule; jurisdiction and recipient type materially change requirements.
At industrial scale, legal and reputation error rates are scaling variables and eligibility belongs before generation/send authorization.
Downstream metrics require very large experiments; causal learning needs hierarchical models, long-horizon outcomes and persistent holdouts.

truthBoundary: This artifact faithfully encodes the material visible in the uploaded 30-page report. It does not fabricate rows from separately referenced downloads that were not embedded in the PDF, does not convert observational associations into causal proof, and does not authorize live outreach.
